Requires careful rank-to-block mapping to respect the lower-bidiagonal dependency (block b needs block b-1 result). Reduces per-iteration communication volume but increases dispatch count (2 collectives × 8 iterations = 16 dispatches).

strategies.name: Two-Phase Hierarchical Aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploit the fact that A[b] and C[b] are global constants: perform the initial all-reduce once, then split the 8 dependent iterations into two phases of 4. First phase computes 4 iterations locally for each rank, exchanges intermediate state via 4 all-reduces, second phase does remaining 4 iterations with 4 more all-reduces. Total 9 dispatches (1 + 4 + 4) with potential for inter-phase fusion.

strategies.name: Pipelined Block-Decomposed Broadcast Chain
strategies.desc:
Since bidiagonal solve is inherently sequential (block b depends on block b-1), pipeline the computation: rank owning block b broadcasts solved result to ranks needing it for block b+1, overlapping broadcast of block b with computation of dependent operations on block b+1. Uses targeted send/recv or broadcast primitives instead of all-reduce, reducing total data movement but increasing dispatch count to ~40 (5 blocks × 8 iterations).
